Traditional Irish Stout

Served at: Saint Patrick's Day

Makes about 1 gallon (3.8 liters) of stoutPrep 30 minCook 4 hours

Stout is a dark, rich beer that is deeply associated with Irish culture and is especially popular during Saint Patrick's Day celebrations. Known for its creamy head and roasted flavors, it is often enjoyed alongside traditional Irish dishes or simply on its own to toast the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 8 lbs (3.6 kg) pale malt extract
  • 1 lb (450 g) roasted barley
  • 1 lb (450 g) flaked barley
  • 0.5 lb (225 g) chocolate malt
  • 1 oz (28 g) East Kent Goldings hops (bittering)
  • 1 oz (28 g) East Kent Goldings hops (aroma)
  • 1 packet Irish ale yeast
  • 5 gallons (19 L) water

Method

  1. Heat 2.5 gallons (9.5 L) of water in a large pot to about 160°F (71°C).
  2. Add roasted barley, flaked barley, and chocolate malt in a grain bag and steep in the water for 30 minutes, maintaining temperature between 150-160°F (65-71°C).
  3. Remove the grain bag and bring the liquid to a boil.
  4. Remove from heat and stir in the pale malt extract until fully dissolved.
  5. Return to a boil and add 1 oz (28 g) of East Kent Goldings hops for bittering. Boil for 60 minutes.
  6. Add the remaining 1 oz (28 g) of hops in the last 5 minutes of the boil for aroma.
  7. Cool the wort quickly to about 70°F (21°C) using an ice bath or wort chiller.
  8. Transfer the wort to a sanitized fermenter and add additional water to reach 5 gallons (19 L).
  9. Pitch the Irish ale yeast and ferment at 65-70°F (18-21°C) for about 2 weeks.
  10. After fermentation is complete, bottle or keg the stout and condition for 2-3 weeks before serving.

Tips

  • Use roasted barley carefully to avoid excessive bitterness; adjust quantity to taste.
  • For a creamier head, consider adding nitrogen when serving, mimicking traditional Irish stouts.
  • Serve chilled but not too cold, around 50-55°F (10-13°C), to appreciate the flavors fully.
